speaker: Sheldon
text: Your questionnaire, very disappointing. You answered the multiple choice questions in a pattern. It's A, B, B, A, C, A, B, B, A, C.

speaker: Leonard
text: I answered every question, Sheldon. Oh, you picked up on that, huh?

speaker: Sheldon
text: How could I not?

speaker: Leonard
text: Come on, there's over 200 questions. And look at some of these things. Sheldon is to camaraderie as the space shuttle is to blank.

speaker: Sheldon
text: There are a number of acceptable answers. For example, C, near Earth transorbital, certainly not B, avocado rancher. And your essay suggesting that I'd have better luck making friends if I wait till the Cylons take over?

speaker: Sheldon
text: Please.

speaker: Leonard
text: John, I put some real work into that.

speaker: Sheldon
text: Yes, well, it's better than what Walowich did. He drew a raccoon with what appears to be a distended scrotum.

speaker: Leonard
text: It's kind of cute. Until you get to the scrotum.

speaker: Sheldon
text: What hope do I have for establishing new relationships, given that my current friends apparently could not take a few hours out of their lives to help me?

speaker: Leonard
text: I'm not going to defend a big bald raccoon.

speaker: Sheldon
text: Well, I don't see how you could.

speaker: Leonard
text: What I'm trying to say is that maybe you can't approach this as a purely intellectual exercise.

speaker: Sheldon
text: What do you mean?

speaker: Leonard
text: Well, remember when you tried to learn how to swim using the internet?

speaker: Sheldon
text: I did learn how to swim. On the floor. The skills are transferable. I just have no interest in going in the water.

speaker: Leonard
text: Then why learn how to swim?

speaker: Sheldon
text: The ice caps are melting, Leonard. In the future, swimming isn't going to be optional. But you do bring up an interesting point. I don't have to break new ground here. I'm sure much of the research already exists.

speaker: Leonard
text: No, no, my point is, if you want to learn how to make friends, then just go out to a coffee shop or a museum, meet people, talk to them, take an interest in their lives.

speaker: Sheldon
text: That's insane on the face of it. Come on. You're driving me to the mall. I'm going to acquire a book that summarizes the current theories in the field of friend-making.

speaker: Leonard
text: Where are we going?

speaker: Leonard
text: You can't just lie down on the floor and swim there.
